description: Reviewed adjudications of the UK local binding fences (uk_local_target_census.json binding_fences). Binding a target family whose fence has no in-force entry here fails in the rowwise doctrine solve before any solve runs. Keys are fence ids; the reason states the ruling (accept the stated basis, or replace it with the named alternative) and cites the evidence.

census_disclosure_control_noise.reason: Accept the stated basis: constituency and local-authority household counts bind to the published disclosure-controlled census values compiled from the pinned Chronicle feed (ons.census.households: ONS TS041 PCON24/LAD, NRS UV404 UKPC24 and council all-occupied totals, NISRA PCON24/LGD14). Per-area dispersion of the retired OA-ladder sums against the published cells at review: England mean 7.4 / max 29, Wales 6.4 / 15, Scotland net −557 (NRS applies disclosure control per output level; same shortfall at both grains), Northern Ireland mean 7 / max 16 after the NI constituency leg moved to NISRA's published DZ2021→PARLCON24 lookup (the earlier postcode inference was a mapping defect of 10 Data Zones, max 694, not perturbation). When a same-concept control is bound above them, the standing cross-grain rule declared in uk_runtime.ledger_targets reconciles each leg to its nearest covering control (country or region since microcosm#905). The census cells count the occupied-household universe and pair only through the household-composition bridge, never with dwelling stock; that cross-grain rescale applies once the bridge is bound. Bound from microcosm#791 (2026-09-11): the three ONS household-composition cells that held the bridge reviewed-unbound now bind on the frs_relationships household type, so the cross-grain rescale runs on the A15-uprated cells; the ten-cell partition and the A15 control are both ons.households_total, so the declared factor is 1 by closure and the receipt records the bridge as bound. Fence evidence: uk_local_target_census.json#/binding_fences/census_disclosure_control_noise; the published cells preserve the source cell-key controls. Re-worded 2026-09-10 (microcosm#887 review round 1); re-worded 2026-09-11 (microcosm#791: the three composition cells re-bound, bridge bound). Re-worded 2026-09-15 (microcosm#929: region controls). Re-worded 2026-10-14 (microcosm#1278): since microcosm#1198 the constituency and local-authority cells reconcile to the nation household controls (England's regions from the Labour Force Survey, Scotland from National Records of Scotland, Wales from the Welsh Government estimate rolled forward by population, Northern Ireland from the census rolled forward by dwelling stock), and A15 targets their sum.
census_disclosure_control_noise.adjudication: microcosm#802; renewed three months on 2026-10-14 by juaristi22 (microcosm#1278): the published cells are still disclosure-controlled, and they now reconcile to the nation household controls.

hmrc_spi_frame_model_proxy.reason: Accept the stated basis: the constituency and local-authority HMRC families bind on the modeled income_tax_annual > 0 frame (each person's income tax over the 12 months before their FRS interview, a proxy for the tax year), the same SPI-frame proxy the national hmrc.* surface binds through (uk_population_targets.json bindings), so both grains share one frame and the standing cross-grain rule can reconcile them. The proxy's known biases (zero-liability taxpayers excluded; modeled liabilities the SPI would not observe included) are accepted for the first candidate and re-measured per family in the microcosm#762 receipts. Fence evidence: uk_local_target_census.json#/binding_fences/hmrc_spi_frame_model_proxy.
hmrc_spi_frame_model_proxy.adjudication: microcosm#762 (A1, rulings 2026-09-02); renewed three months on 2026-10-14 by juaristi22 (microcosm#1278): both grains still bind the HMRC area families on the modeled taxpayer frame; re-worded 2026-10-23 by juaristi22 (microcosm#1347 review): the frame is each person's year of income (income_tax_annual > 0) at both grains, since microcosm#1344 moved the national rows and microcosm#1347 the area rows.

full_frs_tei_band_unavailable.reason: Accept the stated basis: the hmrc_income_by_area family binds the unbanded per-area employment and self-employment amount/count references (count_x_mean over the SPI by-area record sets) and, since microcosm#1198, the higher rate taxpayer counts, which HMRC classes by the marginal rate paid rather than by a total-income band; the published by-area SPI facts carry no total-income band dimension, so no Total-Income-banded local reference exists or may be minted while the 208 national banded facts remain fenced exclusions of the HMRC replay classification. Fence evidence: uk_local_target_census.json#/binding_fences/full_frs_tei_band_unavailable; membership: local_target_reference_membership.json (no banded target ids).
full_frs_tei_band_unavailable.adjudication: microcosm#762 (A1, rulings 2026-09-02); renewed three months on 2026-10-14 by juaristi22 (microcosm#1278): the by-area SPI facts still carry no total-income band.

population_universe_private_households.reason: Accept the stated basis: age-structure targets at constituency and local-authority grain bind the mid-year total-usual-resident universe as published (mid-2025 for local authorities, mid-2024 for constituencies; microcosm#1198), the same universe the national ons.population.age_*_by_region controls bind, so any cross-grain reconciliation happens on one universe. The private-household vs communal-establishment gap (about 1.8% of population in Census 2021, concentrated in the 20-29 and 80+ bands) is recorded as the expected direction of residual error and is not rescaled locally; a declared communal-establishment adjustment would be a chronicle fact request, never a runtime correction. Fence evidence: uk_local_target_census.json#/binding_fences/population_universe_private_households. Re-worded 2026-10-14 (microcosm#1278): the communal-establishment residents by age the adjustment needs are now Chronicle facts (ONS RM120, NRS UV101a, NISRA CT0105), and microcosm#1278 plans the declared adjustment at every grain, national controls included, so that reconciliation still runs on one universe.
population_universe_private_households.adjudication: microcosm#762 (A1, rulings 2026-09-02); renewed three months on 2026-10-14 by juaristi22 (microcosm#1278): pending the age-universe change, which moves every age target to the private-household universe and then retires this entry.

uc_unit_vs_household_grain.reason: Replace the stated basis with the named alternative: the uc_households family binds at benefit-unit grain. uc_households per area counts UC benefit units mapped to their households (the DWP claim-household definition) and the four children bands classify each UC benefit unit by its own num_children (benunit-to-household sum), matching the national dwp.uc.households* re-bind of PR #813; the household-children basis is retired. Fence evidence: uk_local_target_census.json#/binding_fences/uc_unit_vs_household_grain; runtime: microcosm.build.uk_runtime.local_targets.compute_household_metrics. Since the abf0921 re-pin the area series count paid claims, as the national rows do, and the bridge moves the areas by about 0.1%, refusing a factor more than 2% from one at either grain (microcosm#1300).
uc_unit_vs_household_grain.adjudication: microcosm#762 (A1, rulings 2026-09-02); renewed three months on 2026-10-14 by juaristi22 (microcosm#1278): the benefit-unit grain stands; re-worded 2026-10-17 by juaristi22 (microcosm#1302 review): the area series count paid claims since the abf0921 re-pin.

voa_dwellings_vs_household_frame.reason: Re-adjudicated onto the councils' taxbase returns (microcosm#929, plan approved 2026-09-15): the band cells bind the dwellings the councils charge, not the VOA valuation-list stock. England binds MHCLG CTB line 7 minus lines 11 and 15 (chargeable dwellings after the disabled-relief adjustment, less second homes and empty dwellings; band A adds the A- column) per billing authority; Wales binds StatsWales CT1 a1 minus h7 minus h8 by band A-I; Scotland binds CTAXBASE chargeable dwellings per council, the concept its country rows already bound. Measured before the change on the 10 September dense rebuild, the VOA basis ran 6.3 % over the England household rows (0.97-1.20x per authority, median 1.05x) and 6.6 % over Wales, which is where the family's uniform negative bias came from; the taxbase basis leaves England and Wales within about 1 % of the occupied-household frame and Scotland at +1.2 % (chargeable dwellings include some without a resident household). That residual is the expected gap this fence licenses; a country or region control of the same basis reconciles each leg under the standing cross-grain rule. Fence evidence: uk_local_target_census.json#/binding_fences/voa_dwellings_vs_household_frame; lineage: uk-data#371, uk-data#457, microcosm#147 A3, microcosm#762 A1.
voa_dwellings_vs_household_frame.adjudication: microcosm#929 (basis ruling 2026-09-15, replacing microcosm#762 A1 of 2026-09-02); renewed three months on 2026-10-14 by juaristi22 (microcosm#1278): the taxbase basis is unchanged.

high_value_home_stock_derived_estimate.reason: Accepted as the family's basis (microcosm#1240, plan approved 2026-10-13): no publisher counts owner-occupied dwellings above value thresholds by constituency or local authority, and Chronicle registers the Land Registry inputs raw-only (chronicle#343). The estimate's assumptions are declared in the fence and receipted in uk/high_value_home_stock.provenance.json (coverage ratios, the census-implied and controlled owner shares, the uprating fallback counts, the national counts beside the OBR costing note's table 1.1 and the no-correction sensitivities). Where it binds (microcosm#1301, plan approved 2026-10-16): the nine English regions and Wales (microcosm.high_value_homes.over_*_by_region, local line only) control the family; the local-authority cells bind where the derived stock is at least 400 homes (small-cell rule hvcts_la_household_floor in uk/local_small_cell_rule.json), the rest counting in their region row through reconciliation; and the constituency cells are deferred level-wide (high_value_homes_constituency_grain_deferred). Renew on the first dense build's receipts: with the region rows bound the regional 2m-plus shares are fitted and no longer test the basis, so the seat rank correlations against the derived stock and VOA band H, now out of sample, decide whether it stands. Fence: uk_local_target_census.json#/binding_fences/high_value_home_stock_derived_estimate; membership: local_target_reference_membership.json (the high_value_homes/over_* ids at local_authority grain, England and Wales, and their deferred constituency cells) and target_reference_membership.json (the three by-region ids).
high_value_home_stock_derived_estimate.adjudication: microcosm#1240 plan approved by María on 2026-10-13; where the family binds amended by the microcosm#1301 plan she approved on 2026-10-16

desnz_subnational_consumption_basis.reason: Accepted as the family's basis (microcosm#1207, plan approved 2026-10-14): the authority and constituency kWh cells bind DESNZ's split between areas (the constituency cells split the authorities' totals, microcosm#1095) at the lcfs stage's level, one factor per fuel (desnz.energy_trends.gb_domestic_level: Energy Trends for gas, and for electricity the kWh ONS household spending buys at QEP prices, microcosm#1418); DESNZ's own level (electricity read from 31 January to 30 January on non-half-hourly meters and over the calendar year on half-hourly meters; gas mid-May to mid-May and weather-corrected) is not bound. Great Britain's part of the stage's UK level is its share of DESNZ's sub-national consumption with Northern Ireland's all-domestic row added, whose electricity runs on financial years and gas on Northern Ireland gas years, figures DESNZ calls not directly comparable with Great Britain's (microcosm#1278). Renew on the first dense build's receipts: the share of authority cells within 10% and 25% per fuel. Fence: uk_local_target_census.json#/binding_fences/desnz_subnational_consumption_basis.
desnz_subnational_consumption_basis.adjudication: microcosm#1207 plan approved by María on 2026-10-14; fences approved 2026-10-15; re-worded 2026-10-17 by juaristi22 (microcosm#1306 review): the Northern Ireland sentence, since the interim household share it replaced retired (microcosm#1278); re-worded 2026-10-26 by juaristi22 (microcosm#1095): the constituency grain; re-worded 2026-10-28 by juaristi22 (microcosm#1418): electricity's level

desnz_meters_for_households.reason: Accepted (microcosm#1207, plan approved 2026-10-14): gas meters over electricity meters stand for the share of an area's households on the gas network (a constituency's meters split from its authorities'), the ratio the lcfs stage already imposes by region; the census households carry the level through the census partition. Renew on R1: the gas-connected share stays within 0.5 points of DESNZ's. Fence: uk_local_target_census.json#/binding_fences/desnz_meters_for_households.
desnz_meters_for_households.adjudication: microcosm#1207 plan approved by María on 2026-10-14; fences approved 2026-10-15; re-worded 2026-10-26 by juaristi22 (microcosm#1095): the constituency grain

desnz_regional_meter_share_in_stage.reason: Accepted (microcosm#1207, plan approved 2026-10-14): the authority and constituency cells constrain the quantity the stage set by region and add the split between areas; the kWh cells sit on the level the stage raked to. Renew with the first dense build. Fence: uk_local_target_census.json#/binding_fences/desnz_regional_meter_share_in_stage.
desnz_regional_meter_share_in_stage.adjudication: microcosm#1207 plan approved by María on 2026-10-14; fences approved 2026-10-15; re-worded 2026-10-26 by juaristi22 (microcosm#1095): the constituency grain

desnz_small_area_split_for_constituencie.reason: Accepted as the seat cells' basis (microcosm#1095, plan approved 2026-10-25): the constituency cells bind Microcosm's split of each authority's DESNZ total by DESNZ's LSOA and data zone figures (uk/desnz_constituency_energy_facts.json), which keeps every authority's total; a census household split was measured and refused (seats' gas off by a median 4% and up to 38% against the small-area split). Renew on the first dense build that binds the seat cells: the share of seat cells within 10% and 25% per fuel. Fence: uk_local_target_census.json#/binding_fences/desnz_small_area_split_for_constituencies.
desnz_small_area_split_for_constituencie.adjudication: microcosm#1095 plan approved by María on 2026-10-25; fence approved 2026-10-26; the best-fit and gas-connected sentences added to the fence the same day after Vahid's review (microcosm#1404)
